hazard_consequence_node.label: HazardConsequence
hazard_consequence_node.name: Toxicity dispersion
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: “On February 12, 2014, two employees ... suffered first and second degree chemical burns ... concentrated sulfuric acid sprayed two workers following a mechanical integrity failure ... This resulted in the release of approximately 84,000 pounds of sulfuric acid.”
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: The incident centers on a large loss of containment of sulfuric acid that sprayed workers and released hazardous acid to the environment for over two hours. No ignition, fire, explosion, or oxygen-deficient atmosphere occurred. Among the allowed categories, Toxicity dispersion is the best fit for this harmful chemical release mechanism.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: Sulfuric acid
entity_nodes.evidence: concentrated sulfuric acid sprayed two workers
entity_nodes.explanation: Sulfuric acid was the hazardous material released from the sampling system and it directly caused the workers' chemical burn injuries.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: Liquid
condition_nodes.evidence: concentrated sulfuric acid sprayed two workers
condition_nodes.explanation: The released sulfuric acid was in liquid form and sprayed from the failed tubing connection.

condition_nodes.label: Pressure
condition_nodes.name: Low pressure
condition_nodes.evidence: operating below 100 pounds per square inch gauge (psig)
condition_nodes.explanation: The source vessel was operating below 100 psig, indicating a relatively low-pressure release rather than a high-pressure event.

condition_nodes.label: Temperature
condition_nodes.name: Atmospheric temperature
condition_nodes.evidence: near the ambient temperature of approximately 50 degrees Fahrenheit
condition_nodes.explanation: The sulfuric acid was released near ambient conditions rather than at unusually high or low process temperature.

condition_nodes.label: ToxicSubstance
condition_nodes.name: Toxic
condition_nodes.evidence: acid fumes are harmful if inhaled
condition_nodes.explanation: The report describes sulfuric acid fumes as harmful if inhaled and the released acid caused worker injuries, supporting classification as a toxic substance.

condition_nodes.label: ReleaseType
condition_nodes.name: Continuous release
condition_nodes.evidence: acid continued to spray out of the failed tubing for over two hours
condition_nodes.explanation: The sulfuric acid discharge continued for an extended period until responders isolated the system, so the release was continuous rather than instantaneous.

condition_nodes.label: Dispersion
condition_nodes.name: Dispersed
condition_nodes.evidence: spraying the two operators with acid
condition_nodes.explanation: The failed connection produced an acid spray that dispersed hazardous material into the surrounding work area.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Opening the valve to return the sulfuric acid sampling system to service following maintenance
event_nodes.evidence: The incident occurred when the operators opened a valve to return an acid sampling system back to service.
event_nodes.explanation: The initiating event was the start-up action that reintroduced sulfuric acid into the repaired sampling system.

event_nodes.label: MechanicalFailure
event_nodes.name: ¾-inch stainless steel tubing connector came apart due to insufficient tightening at a compression joint
event_nodes.evidence: failure of a ¾-inch diameter stainless steel tubing connector that came apart due to insufficient tightening between a tube and a compression joint
event_nodes.explanation: This connector failure was the direct mechanical integrity breakdown that caused the sulfuric acid loss of containment.
